items.title: Understanding clinical reasoning variability in medical large language models: a mechanistic interpretability study
items.abstract: Medical large language models (LLMs) achieving high benchmark accuracy exhibit unexplained variability in clinical tasks, producing errors that clinicians cannot safeguard against. We evaluated clinical reasoning stability in GPT-5, MedGemma-27B-Text-IT, and OpenBioLLM-Llama3-70B using 355 systematic perturbations of physician-validated oncology cases and trained sparse autoencoders on 1 billion tokens from 50,000 MIMIC-IV clinical notes to decompose their internal representation. We find models exhibit dramatic reasoning instability, shifting staging accuracy by over 50% based solely on prompt format, or generating definitive staging in clinically insufficient scenarios. Sparse autoencoder analysis revealed hierarchical encoding in MedGemma, where high-magnitude features encode lexical identity and low-magnitude features encode contextual meaning. OpenBioLLM distributes information uniformly. We demonstrate these internal encoding structures differentially affect retrieval interventions, suggesting interventions effective for one architecture may harm another. We recommend healthcare institutions implement architecture-specific safety validation, as benchmark equivalence does not imply functional equivalence, with implications for AI safety beyond healthcare.

items.title: USER-CENTERED DESIGN IN WARDROBES: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
items.abstract: The wardrobe, as a fundamental component of domestic space, mediates the daily ritual of clothing selection, storage, and self-presentation, yet its design has historically been driven by manufacturing conventions rather than systematic engagement with user needs. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this systematic review conducted a comprehensive literature search across Scopus and Web of Science. After strict screening based on inclusion and exclusion criteria, 68 high-quality studies were finally included for systematic coding and thematic synthesis. Thematic synthesis yielded seven interconnected themes: user needs and requirements, ergonomic design, cognitive and behavioral dimensions, smart and intelligent wardrobes, customization and modular systems, accessibility and inclusive design, and cultural and aesthetic considerations. Findings reveal that UCD methods can substantially improve wardrobe usability, accessibility, and user satisfaction, yet the literature remains fragmented across disciplinary silos, methodologically constrained by short-duration laboratory studies. Three critical research gaps are identified: the absence of longitudinal field studies, insufficient participant diversity, limited real-world validation of smart wardrobe prototypes, poor integration across thematic domains, and neglect of sustainability as a design dimension. The review concludes by articulating a forward-looking research agenda and practical guidance for designers, manufacturers, and educators seeking to place the user at the center of wardrobe design.

items.title: Using AI in Book Writing with Human Supervision: A Case Study in Astronomy for Kids
items.abstract: In recent years, the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI) and creative writing has opened new possibilities in producing educational content. This paper explores the process of co-authoring a children's book on astronomy using AI as a writing assistant, under the supervision of a subject matter expert. While AI has advanced significantly in generating coherent, relevant text, human guidance is crucial to ensure scientific accuracy, pedagogical appropriateness, and an engaging narrative tailored to young readers. In this case study, I, the principal author and co-creator, utilized AI writing tools to draft a book aimed at children aged 7 to 14, explaining key astronomical concepts in an accessible and engaging way. The book, titled “Los Fundamentos de la Astronomia" was framed within the context of Colombia's night sky, making it both regionally relevant and scientifically sound. The project originated from my attendance at an astronomy conference in Athens, Greece, where I met José, a Colombian astronomer who described the challenges of teaching astronomy in Colombia using textbooks written from a European perspective. The positional differences in celestial observations between Spain and Colombia created significant confusion for his students. Recognizing an opportunity to address this regional educational gap, I proposed a collaboration using AI as a tool combined with his astronomical expertise to create culturally appropriate educational materials. items.title: Weak-Signal Intelligence: An AI-Enabled Intelligent Modeling Framework for Early Detection of Strategic Disruptions
items.abstract: Strategic environments are increasingly characterized by uncertainty, rapid technological change, and disruptions that may initially appear as low-visibility or ambiguous signals. Existing approaches to weak-signal analysis, strategic foresight, early-warning systems, and artificial intelligence address parts of this challenge but remain fragmented, particularly in connecting signal detection with interpretation and strategic assessment. This study develops Weak-Signal Intelligence (WSI) as an AI-enabled organizational capability for detecting, interpreting, integrating, and evaluating weak signals to anticipate emerging strategic disruptions. Using a conceptual theory-building and intelligent modeling approach, the study integrates insights from weak-signal research, strategic foresight, early-warning systems, artificial intelligence, sensemaking, uncertainty, and complexity. The proposed framework connects signal detection, interpretation, pattern recognition, uncertainty analytics, disruption assessment, strategic response intelligence, and adaptive learning. The model positions WSI as a continuous human–AI process that transforms low-visibility signals into uncertainty-aware strategic early-warning intelligence. The study contributes a conceptual foundation for improving strategic awareness and preparedness and provides directions for future empirical validation, measurement development, and cross-sector application.

items.title: Web-Based and Mobile AI Tools in Southeast Asian Higher Education: A Systematic Review and Thematic Synthesis
items.abstract: Web-based and mobile artificial intelligence tools have spread rapidly in Southeast Asian universities, yet evidence on what they achieved in real learning remained fragmented. This systematic review synthesised empirical studies that implemented or evaluated such tools in degree-level higher education in Southeast Asia between 2021 and 2026. Following the PRISMA 2020 guideline, 642 Scopus records were screened, 79 full texts were assessed and 59 studies were included. Study quality was appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, measured outcomes were summarised by effect direction, and findings were integrated through three-stage thematic synthesis. Most studies came from Indonesia, Vietnam and Thailand, concerned language learning, used general-purpose chatbots and relied on non-randomised designs. Of 45 studies that measured learning, 36 reported improvements, mainly in uncontrolled designs or against routine teaching, whereas four of six comparisons with equivalent human support found no difference. Five analytical themes emerged: polished products with uncertain learning, pedagogy over presence, an affective double edge, unequal readiness and comparator-dependent conclusions. The evidence supported these tools as comparable and scalable complements within teacher-mediated, bounded designs rather than as superior replacements. The review proposed an orchestration framework and a research agenda that prioritised active comparators and independent, delayed measures of learning.

items.title: When adaptation has no endpoint: cognitive flexibility under prolonged organizational strain
items.abstract: Purpose This paper examines how cognition operates under conditions of prolonged organizational strain where demands persist, interpretations do not converge and disengagement does not occur. It challenges the dominant assumption in organizational behavior that cognitive processes under strain are inherently directional and oriented toward resolution, coherence or withdrawal. Design/methodology/approach The paper develops a conceptual framework through integrative analysis of stress and coping, sensemaking and burnout literatures. It identifies a shared directional assumption across these perspectives and demonstrates its limitations under conditions of sustained and indeterminate strain. A new construct is introduced and formalized through a set of theoretical propositions. Findings The analysis shows that individuals may sustain cognitive engagement without reducing demands, achieving interpretive coherence or disengaging. To account for this pattern, the paper introduces cognitive flexibility under prolonged organizational strain, defined as a mode of functioning characterized by interpretive openness, non-directional engagement and ongoing meaning adjustment without convergence. Originality/value The paper contributes by identifying prolonged organizational strain as a distinct condition and re-specifying adaptation as sustained cognitive functioning without directional progression. It extends organizational behavior theory by explaining how cognition operates when resolution, coherence and disengagement do not structure activity.

items.title: When Algorithms Set Prices: Emerging Consumer Fairness Challenges in AI-Driven Dynamic Pricing
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is turning dynamic pricing from a standardized management decision into an individual, algorithmic experience. Algorithmic pricing improves efficiency and personalization, but its opacity and individualized prices can leave consumers feeling treated unfairly and distrustful. This short communication draws on recent research on algorithmic pricing, price fairness, price transparency, and consumer trust to build a conceptual framework. It links four features of algorithmic pricing (real-time adaptation, personalization, individualized price differentiation, and limited explainability) to perceived price fairness, which in turn shapes consumer trust and acceptance or resistance. The paper argues that fairness is a strategic management problem, not only an ethical concern. Implications for pricing managers cover price explanations, responsible personalization, and governance, and empirical research directions are proposed.

items.title: Work-Related Burnout, Insomnia, and Psychological Well-Being among Computer Programmers: A Correlational Study in Lahore, Pakistan
items.abstract: Background: Computer programmers face intensive cognitive demands, sustained concentration, tight deadlines, and extended working hours that may compromise occupational health. This study examined relationships among work-related burnout, insomnia, and psychological well-being among computer programmers in Lahore, Pakistan. Methods: A cross-sectional correlational study recruited 250 employed programmers, comprising 143 men and 107 women, aged 18–35 years. Data were collected between April and June 2024 through face-to-face questionnaires and Google Forms. Participants completed the Oldenburg Burnout Inventory, Bergen Insomnia Scale, and Psychological Well-Being Scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, simple linear regression, and independent-samples t tests in SPSS 23. Results: Burnout correlated positively with insomnia (r = .248, p < .01) and negatively with psychological well-being (r = −.159, p < .05). The insomnia–well-being correlation was nonsignificant (r = −.053, p = .401). Burnout explained 6.2% of insomnia variance and 2.5% of psychological well-being variance. Women reported significantly higher burnout (p = .005) and insomnia (p = .022) than men; their psychological well-being scores did not differ significantly (p = .108). Conclusion: Greater burnout was associated with more insomnia symptoms and modestly poorer psychological well-being among programmers. Occupational workload management and access to employee support deserve attention. Because this study was cross-sectional and relied on self-report measures, the findings should not be interpreted as evidence of causal relationships.

items.title: Writing Parameters for 3D Printing of Dental Prostheses by Optimizing Them Using AI
items.abstract: Abstract We saw that the parameters for a dental printing process have a significant influence on the quality of the dental printed part, such as the layer height, speed of printing, orientation of printing, exposure time, and some parameters related to the used resin. There are many tra ditional ways of choosing the parameters, which are mostly empirical, and consequently lead to errors of dimensions, flaws on surfaces, and high consumption of material; there is also high production time. An Artificial Intelligence (AI) supported optimization scheme is proposed here for the optimal selection of 3D printing parameters to increase the quality and the production efficiency of individual dental prostheses. The proposed approach consists of data acquisition, data collection/preprocessing, feature analysis, training of the machine learning models, and optimization of the parameters to find out correlation between the printing conditions and quality factors such as dimensional accuracy, surface roughness, manufacturing time and con sumption of the materials. Various performance metrics are employed to analyze the different machine learning models and then the best one is utilized to determine the optimum parameter. There are plans to minimize the trial and error methods and to select the parameters on a data driven basis.

items.title: Yojna AI : AI Government Scheme Recommendation System for Citizen Eligibility and Assistance
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) can simplify access to government welfare schemes by helping citizens identify schemes relevant to their needs and eligibility. This paper presents YojanaAI, an AI-based Government Scheme Recommendation System designed to support scheme discovery and eligibility assessment using user-specific information. The system aims to simplify the process of identifying suitable schemes based on relevant attributes such as age, income, occupation, and education. It provides a structured approach to accessing scheme details, eligibility requirements, and application information. The proposed system focuses on improving information accessibility and reducing the effort required to search multiple sources. Its effectiveness can be assessed through eligibility-matching accuracy, recommendation relevance, and usability testing. The paper outlines the proposed approach, potential applications, limitations, and future enhancements for developing accessible and citizen-centric digital public services.

items.abstract: The article substantiates the feasibility of adaptive foreign language phonetics teaching, enhanced by artificial intelligence technologies, as an alternative to traditional standardized methods that fail to account for higher education students' individual articulatory features and lead to persistent phonetic errors. The study is interdisciplinary, combining the methodology of specialties A4 Secondary Education (A4.021 English Language and Literature), A5 Vocational Education (A5.39 Digital Technologies), and F7 Computer Engineering. The purpose of the study is to develop and justify a model of an adaptive learning platform for improving higher education students' phonetic skills through the integration of speech formant synthesis with machine learning algorithms. A formant synthesizer model based on parallel digital filters has been developed, generating reference vowel sounds by simulating the resonant frequencies of the vocal tract. An approach to personalizing learning is proposed based on a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network, which analyzes a student's error history and dynamically adjusts formant parameters in real time. Technical validation of the model demonstrated high accuracy of formant frequency correction, with a root-mean-square error of 45 Hz for the first formant and 78 Hz for the second, enabling objective assessment of pronunciation quality and adaptation of exercise difficulty to the individual student's level. A pilot quasi-experimental verification of the platform involving experimental and control groups of higher education students confirmed its pedagogical potential for implementing differentiated learning principles based on objective acoustic data. The conclusions confirm the platform's prospects for modernizing linguistic education. Further research directions include expanding empirical validation on a larger sample and conducting perceptual evaluation of synthesized speech quality by native speakers to confirm its naturalness and suitability for learning purposes.

items.abstract: Rapid digitalization in higher education, combined with the need for universities to operate under geographically distributed and relocated conditions, highlights a crucial shift from rigid hierarchical management to flexible, decentralized systems. This paper substantiates the architecture of decentralized university management models driven by multi-agent systems and large language models (LLMs), presenting its architectural justification and functional implementation within a higher education institution. The study details theoretical foundations of utilizing multi-agent systems, orchestration protocols, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and vector databases to optimize university workflows under conditions of limited observability and distributed IT infrastructure. The methodology rests on a two-tier multi-agent architecture, where dynamic request routing is achieved through a hierarchical orchestration model using AgentSpec formal specifications, while action consistency is maintained by a central algorithmic coordinator. Findings indicate that deploying a standalone autonomous agent for each of the university’s 24 departments is inefficient due to risks of algorithmic conflicts, redundant queries to the vector knowledge base, increased LLM hallucination rates, and context window constraints. To address these limitations, a coordinated multi-agent architecture was implemented at Kherson State University. This framework consolidates operations into five core macro-agents—academic affairs, administrative management, knowledge management, educational quality assurance, and communications—managed by a Central Orchestrator routing queries, controlling access privileges, and synthesizing analytical outputs. The paper identifies key organizational and technological hurdles, focusing on maintaining high levels of trust, decision verification, and role-based access control during delegation. Finally, it outlines the roadmap for evolving this framework into a university digital twin capable of predictive modeling and automated process support. These findings offer practical value for higher education institutions deploying digital ecosystems under human resource, infrastructural, and security constraints.

items.abstract: Recent years have witnessed rapid advances in generative artificial intelligence (AI) models such as ChatGPT and Gemini, opening new prospects for supporting the educational process. This study aims to measure the effectiveness of generative AI models in improving university students' academic writing skills, using a quasi-experimental design with experimental and control groups (N = 60 second-year students of the Faculty of Education, randomly assigned to the two groups). The experimental group received a six-week training program that integrated generative AI as a writing assistant across brainstorming, drafting, language revision, and referencing, while the control group followed traditional instruction. An academic writing skills test and an observation checklist were used as instruments. The study hypothesizes statistically significant differences (α = 0.05) favoring the experimental group in thesis clarity, idea organization, linguistic accuracy, and academic referencing, alongside positive attitudes toward AI as a supportive tool rather than a substitute for thinking. In addition, an exploratory descriptive survey of 87 university students found that 93.1% had previously used generative AI tools for academic writing, 95.4% supported clear university policies governing their use, and 72.4% reported concern about over-reliance on them. The study recommends training faculty members to integrate generative AI tools into academic writing courses and establishing an ethical charter to govern their use.

items.abstract: Traditional circuit breakers provide protection against overcurrent and short-circuit conditions but have no inherent provision for remote supervision, demand awareness or intelligent load management. This paper introduces the design, implementation and experimental testing of a smart circuit breaker that combines independent electrical protection, hybrid Global System for Mobile communication (GSM)–Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity, and an energy optimization layer based on artificial intelligence (AI). An edge controller measures voltage, current, active power and energy in real time and publishes telemetry through a Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) link or, when Internet connectivity is lost, through the GSM short-message service (SMS). A hybrid Long Short-Term Memory–Extreme Gradient Boosting (LSTM–XGBoost) model forecasts short-term demand, and a weighted objective function schedules deferrable loads to minimize electricity cost and peak demand while satisfying circuit-capacity and user-priority constraints. Software and communication functions never substitute for hardware protection; a certified miniature circuit breaker (MCB) remains the primary fault-interruption device. the prototype measured the electrical quantities with a maximum loaded-condition deviation of 0.76% from the calibrated reference values; the forecaster achieved an RMSE of 0.083 kW and a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.9899; and the hybrid channel maintained a 97.1% command-success rate during controlled Internet-outage trials, whereas the IoT-only channel recorded 0%. Compared with conventional operation, the AI-driven strategy reduced peak demand by 39.6% and electricity cost by 8.0%, whereas total energy consumption decreased by only 3.0%, indicating that its main advantage is peak-demand reduction rather than energy reduction. These findings indicate the feasibility of a deployable device that combines protection, resilient communication and predictive energy management.

items.title: ‘Can we have two golds?’ The virtuous potentiality of deliberate medal sharing
items.abstract: In the 2021 Olympics, high jumpers Barshim and Tamberi and in the 2023 World Athletics Championships pole vaulters Moon and Kennedy refused tiebreak procedures (the jump-off) after clearing the same height. The athletes thus shared gold medals. Deliberate jump-off refusals can challenge the conventional Olympic motto (faster, higher, stronger), highlight the significance of ties as meaningful resolutions without privileging participation over victory, and foreground mutualism over self-distinguishing gain. By agreeing to stop together, athletes redefine sporting excellence as shared and as divorced from more-than-human performance; they also reject the imposition to prioritize fan entertainment. Moreover, the acknowledgement of mutual limits underscores a consideration of measure and ultimately of virtue as moderation.

items.title: "Büyük Endüstriyel Kazaların Riskinin Azaltılmasında Tarihsel Evrim: BEKRA ve Seveso Direktifi Uyum Sürecinin Türkiye Açısından Analitik Değerlendirilmesi"
items.abstract: "Major industrial accidents constitute one of the most critical risk areas of modern industrial societies due to their high destructive effects despite their low probabilities of occurrence. Cases throughout history prove that these events arise not only from technical failures, but also from organizational weaknesses, systemic deficiencies, human factors, and inadequately designed safety systems. Root cause analyses reveal that the underlying causes of accidents are the insufficient analysis of reaction kinetics, the failure to correctly evaluate the accident chain developing after the loss of control, and, most importantly, the failure to keep risk analyses up to date. This situation proves that process safety should not be limited only to engineering design; it makes a holistic approach encompassing operational discipline, human factors, and organizational learning capacity necessary. The dioxin release that occurred in the town of Seveso, Italy, as a result of the uncontrolled shutdown of a reactor and the failure to correctly evaluate the by-products that could be released, fundamentally changed the European perspective on industrial safety and paved the way for the issuance of the first Seveso Directive. The Seveso Directives established within the European Union and the Regulation on the Prevention of Major Industrial Accidents and Mitigation of Their Effects (BEKRA Regulation), which entered into force in our country in line with these directives, constitute the fundamental legal and technical infrastructure for the prevention of accidents and minimization of their damages within the scope of technological disaster management. The Bhopal tragedy, which occurred despite the first directive being in force, and the Baia Mare accident, which resulted in environmental damage crossing national borders, became milestones in industrial safety and enabled the principle of “preventability of accidents” to be replaced by a more comprehensive understanding of “risk management.” In this process, critical requirements such as the domino effect, land-use planning, and informing the public were introduced into the directives. Lessons learned from experienced industrial accidents reveal that the “prescriptive” approach alone is not sufficient in the integration of safety management systems into processes. Current requirements make it necessary to adopt a “performance-based” approach that goes beyond the set of rules. Although significant progress has been made in our country in terms of regulatory compliance, there are still areas for improvement regarding process safety culture, organizational learning processes, and the internalization of advanced risk analysis techniques. For effective accident risk management, compliance with only regulatory parameters should not be considered sufficient; a performance-based, holistic, and sustainable process safety strategy should be ensured to permeate all operational processes. It is of critical importance that future studies strengthen interdisciplinary approaches and focus particularly on safety culture and organizational learning processes."

items.title: 200 Years of Children in Literature: On their Visibility, Value, and Agency
items.abstract: Across modern literary history, children have served as powerful symbolic figures through which societies negotiate core social values. Yet despite their prominence in canonical criticism, we lack a systematic account of how often children appear in novels, how they are valued, and what kinds of agency they are afforded over time. To address this gap, I conduct a large-scale computational analysis of 9,544 English-language novels published between 1800 and 2000. This study provides the first large-scale extraction of child characters from the modern novel, combining classical natural language processing with large language models to measure their visibility, emotional valuation, narrative agency, and independence from kinship structures. Contrary to dominant histories of childhood, children and adolescents become progressively less visible in the novel over time, a decline driven by the erosion of the adolescent girl in particular. Children maintain a more positive emotional valence than adults even as their agency lags behind adult peers, suggesting a broader portrait of children as sentimentally valued, yet structurally constrained social actors.

items.title: A Comprehensive Review of Agentic Artificial Intelligence for Autonomous Data Pipeline Management: Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions
items.abstract: The rapid development of cloud technology, big data, and artificial intelligence has changed the way data pipelines are managed in today’s world. Conventional data pipeline management systems depend on rule-based automation and manual intervention making them less effective in managing dynamic workloads, detecting anomalies, recovering from faults, and optimizing resources. The recent advances in Agentic Artificial Intelligence, LLMs, reinforcement learning, and multi-agent systems have given rise to the autonomous systems that can perform monitoring, diagnosis, recovery, and optimization on their own. This review studies the state-of-the-art AI information pipeline management processes, intelligent work flow orchestration, autonomous decision making, and self-healing systems. The paper reviews the existing methodologies, including ETL automation, metadata-based data ingestion, optimization through reinforcement learning, and agent-based orchestration systems, and presents their advantages, limitations, and potential fields of application. Moreover, the review identifies main research problems faced by researchers and developers including explainability, interoperability, scalability, security, and adaptation in heterogeneous cloud environments.

items.title: A CRITICAL REVIEW ON DIGITAL HR TRANSFORMATION AND EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT IN THE ERA OF INDUSTRY 5.0
items.abstract: The shift from Industry 4.0 to Industry 5.0 marks a profound paradigm evolution in strategic human resource management (HRM), transitioning from pure technological automation to human-centric socio-technical synergy, sustainability, and organizational resilience. This critical review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature published between 2021 and 2026 to evaluate the influence of digital HR transformation—encompassing artificial intelligence, predictive people analytics, cloud-based HRIS, and collaborative robotics (cobots)—on multi-dimensional employee engagement (vigor, dedication, and absorption). Guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) framework, 16 benchmark empirical and conceptual studies were systematically selected and categorized. The synthesis reveals that while digital HR transformation significantly drives operational efficiency, its direct impact on employee engagement is mediated by digital fluency, perceived organizational support, and psychological safety. Furthermore, algorithmic transparency and responsible data governance serve as critical moderators that mitigate techno-stress, privacy anxieties, and algorithmic burnout. The paper delivers an integrative socio-technical framework for Industry 5.0, offering strategic guidance for organizational leaders seeking to align cutting-edge HR technologies with human well-being and sustainable performance.

items.title: A CRITICAL REVIEW ON EMPLOYEE WELL-BEING AND SUSTAINABLE HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES
items.abstract: In contemporary organizational research, the imperative to balance economic productivity with human sustainability has elevated Sustainable Human Resource Management (Sustainable HRM) into a core strategic framework. This critical review systematically evaluates 16 benchmark empirical and conceptual studies published between 2021 and 2026 to investigate how Sustainable HRM practices influence tri-dimensional employee well-being (physical, psychological, and social) and long-term organizational performance. Adhering to PRISMA 2020 systematic review protocols, this study synthesizes structural equation modelling (SEM) findings, panel econometrics, and qualitative case studies across diverse industrial and geographical settings. The synthesis reveals that while traditional HRM prioritizes short-term transactional output, Sustainable HRM embeds ergonomic work design, psychological safety, work-life boundary protection, and green employee voice, yielding a significant positive effect on psychological capital (β = 0.44, p < .001) and work-family enrichment (β = 0.41, p < .001). Meta-analyzed structural models demonstrate that physical and psychological well-being fully mediate the relationship between sustainable work practices and employee job performance (β = 0.38, p < .001), while drastically reducing turnover intentions. However, critical gaps persist regarding paradoxical workload pressures under green mandates and regional implementation disparities. This paper presents a multi-level governance framework providing actionable pathways for HR leaders to operationalize sustainable well-being.

items.title: A framework for structuring Thai medical documents using systematized nomenclature of medicine clinical terms and large language models
items.abstract: Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine – Clinical Terms (SNOMED CT) enables semantically interoperable health data, but implementation in Thailand is hindered by language and workflow challenges. We evaluated whether large language models (LLMs) can automate SNOMED CT concept extraction from Thai clinical documents. The objectives of this study are to develop a proof-of-concept framework for automated clinical named entity recognition and SNOMED CT concept linking from Thai medical documents, and to compare the performance and resource requirements of closed-source and open-source LLMs on a human-annotated dataset. The dataset was manually annotated from 220 Thai medical documents (6,390 entities) from three outpatient departments. Our retrieval-augmented framework was evaluated using four LLMs (Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-4.1, Qwen 3, and MedGemma) as experimental based models which were comparatively analyzed for entity recognition using precision, recall, F1 score and concept linking using character-level metric, Intersection over Union (IoU), as well as resource consumptions. For entity recognition, Gemini achieved the highest performance (loose F1 83.31%). For SNOMED CT concept extraction ranked most similar (Top-1) by encoder models for retrieval and re-ranking, IoU scores were 39.42% (Gemini), 34.44% (GPT), 29.86% (MedGemma), and 28.62% (Qwen). Average processing time for end-to-end extraction was 5–6 minutes per document for Gemini and GPT, with cost estimates in United states dollars (USD) of USD 0.035 and USD 0.019 per document, respectively; local open-source inference required up to 10 minutes per document. This study established a proof-of-concept framework for automated clinical entity recognition and SNOMED CT concept linking from Thai medical documents, demonstrating practical LLM performance with trade-offs between accuracy, cost, and efficiency across closed-source and open-source models.

items.title: A General-Purpose Adaptable Foundation Model for Total-Body PET Kinetic Modelling
items.abstract: Voxel-level kinetic modeling in total-body dynamic positron emission tomography (TB-PET) enables precise physiological quantification but complicates parameter uncertainty estimation. While generative consistency models (CMs) can rapidly estimate Bayesian posterior distributions, they are constrained by type of tracers, kinetic models, and protocols. Training them from scratch whenever a new tracer, model or protocol is used can be computationally intensive. To address this, we introduce LoRACM, a parameter-efficient framework utilizing low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to transfer a pretrained foundation CM to novel TB-PET scenarios. We evaluated three adaptation scenarios using simulated and human data: scanner and protocol transfer for FDG two-tissue compartment modeling; FP-CIT simplified reference tissue modeling; and high-temporal-resolution FDG blood flow imaging via the adiabatic approximation to tissue homogeneity model. Each adaptation was trained in less than 3 hours on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU using 50,000 simulated pairs. In simulations, LoRACM showed strong agreement with results from Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC, which we use as reference posterior distributions), yielding median Kullback-Leibler divergences of 0.05-0.11 and median absolute percentage errors below 1.2% for each kinetic parameter of interest. In human data, LoRACM generated total-body K_i maps comparable to the ones made by non-negative nonlinear least squares (NNLS) fitting and a consistency model trained from scratch. Striatal dopamine binding potential estimates predicted by LoRACM correlated with NNLS estimates (r = 0.968-0.988). LoRACM produced total-body blood flow imaging with FDG matching the one made by NNLS. These underscore the potential of adapting a pretrained CM with LoRA for fast and reliable posterior parameter inference for kinetic models across distinct TB-PET applications.

items.title: A Generative AI-Integrated Framework for Teaching Operations Management: Case-Based Projects
items.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GAI) reshapes business education, instructors must simultaneously safeguard academic integrity and develop students’ AI literacy for an increasingly AI-driven workplace. This study developed the GAI Learning Framework (GLF), a replicable, step-by-step experiential learning approach for case-based projects in undergraduate business courses, illustrated through an operations management (OM) application. Rather than enabling passive cognitive offloading, the GLF promotes active learning by requiring students to craft context-rich prompts grounded in course materials, systematically compare outputs across multiple GAI platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini), and critically evaluate discrepancies against independently verified sources. The framework was implemented across two sections of an undergraduate OM course and evaluated using a student survey that combined Likert-scale items with open-ended reflections (n = 50). All three constructs exceeded the scale midpoint, with pooled means ranging from 3.93 (Constructive Alignment) to 4.08 (Cognitive Load/Scaffolding). Qualitative student reflections further indicated that students perceived the framework as fostering active learning, AI platform literacy, and professional communication skills. This study offers educators a practical, classroom-tested framework for integrating GAI tools into case-based projects in business courses while preserving analytical rigor and promoting experiential learning. items.title: A GeoAI framework for landslide susceptibility mapping using Google Earth Engine, ensemble machine learning, and SHAP explainable AI
items.abstract: Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards in mountainous regions, yet susceptibility mapping in data-scarce areas remains challenging. This study proposes a reproducible Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI) framework that integrates Google Earth Engine (GEE), ensemble machine learning, and explainable AI (XAI) for landslide susceptibility mapping in central Nepal. Using a balanced dataset of 9,479 observations from 4,743 landslide and 4,736 non-landslide locations, extracted seven conditioning factors: topographic (elevation, slope, aspect), climatic (rainfall), ecological (NDVI, land cover), and anthropogenic (population density) within the GEE cloud computing environment. Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models using stratified train-test splitting and 10-fold cross-validation. Both models showed strong predictive performance, with XGBoost achieving superior results (Accuracy: 88.3%, ROC-AUC: 0.952) compared to RF (Accuracy: 87.9%, ROC-AUC: 0.945). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified slope as the most influential predictor associated with model predictions followed by rainfall (16%) and elevation (15%), while lower NDVI values consistently correlated with higher susceptibility. The susceptibility map identified high-risk zones concentrated in Sindhupalchok, Dolakha, Dhading, Rasuwa, Gorkha, and Nuwakot districts. This framework reveals that freely available satellite data, cloud computing, and explainable machine learning can be effectively integrated for susceptibility mapping and community resilience initiatives.

items.title: A GeoAI Framework for Offshore Wind Farm Site Suitability Prediction Using Ensemble Machine Learning
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with geospatial analysis, commonly referred to as GeoAI, provides new opportunities for renewable-energy planning and site-suitability assessment. However, limited attention has been given to integrating Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) with machine learning (ML) for offshore wind farm suitability assessment. This study proposes a GeoAI framework to predict offshore wind farm suitability using ensemble machine-learning techniques. A pooled technology-aware ML model was developed using nine predictors, including a turbine type to account for fixed-bottom and floating technologies. Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Logistic Regression were evaluated, with a majority-class classifier included as a baseline. Model development and hyperparameter optimization were conducted using five-fold stratified group cross-validation based on geographic blocks, with weighted F1-score used as the primary model-selection metric. Gradient Boosting achieved the best model, with a weighted F1-score of 0.8077, followed closely by XGBoost (0.8031), and was therefore selected for final evaluation. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis further revealed that wind power density, wind speed, and water depth were the most influential factors governing offshore wind farm suitability predictions.

items.title: A Heuristic Tool to Enable Root Cause Analysis of Safety Events
items.abstract: Background Hospitals routinely collect wide-ranging data related to quality, efficiency, and clinical practice. As part of these efforts, patient safety event data are collected, compiled, and analyzed to drive process improvement. Methods We present a novel adaptation and application of the Department of Defense Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) as a heuristic tool to improve the conduct of root cause analysis (RCA) sessions that follow serious patient safety events. To assess individual knowledge improvement after reviewing the heuristic tool, a 1-page summary (including a graphical image of the tool) was developed and provided to a convenience sample of staff in our facility (N = 48). Participants were asked to read over the information and then answer a 5-question survey about their knowledge of the RCA process. A Likert scale was used to assess participants’ level of knowledge prior to, and following, their exposure to the 1-page summary. Results Mean Likert scores increased from 2.83 to 3.42 (Δ = +0.59), reflecting improved self-reported participant perception of knowledge gained around RCA principles (paired t-test: t(47) = 4.10, P < .001) with a medium effect size (Cohen’s d = 0.59). Conclusion The results from this pilot study suggest that this heuristic tool may improve knowledge of RCA concepts among clinical staff. At higher levels of an organization, improved accuracy and precision of locally entered data would also improve centralized human factor data analysis to inform decision-making.

items.title: A Large Language Model Framework for Seed Implant Brachytherapy: Adaptive Weight Optimization via Retrieval‐Augmented Generation
items.abstract: Seed implant brachytherapy (SIBT) is an effective cancer treatment modality; however, clinical planning often relies on manual adjustment of objective function weights, leading to inefficiencies and suboptimal results. This study proposes an adaptive weight optimization framework for SIBT planning, driven by large language models (LLMs). A locally deployed DeepSeek-R1 LLM is integrated with an automatic planning algorithm in an iterative loop. Starting with fixed weights, the LLM evaluates plan quality and recommends new weights in the next iteration. This process continues until convergence criteria are met, after which the LLM conducts a comprehensive evaluation to identify the optimal plan. A clinical knowledge base, constructed and queried via retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), enhances the model's domain-specific reasoning. The proposed method was retrospectively validated on 23 patient cases who underwent head-and-neck SIBT, showing that the LLM-assisted approach maintained clinical target volume (CTV) coverage and reduced excessive target dose relative to fixed-weight planning; in the eight patients with available organs at risk (OARs) contours, OAR dose metrics showed favorable numerical trends. The study demonstrates the potential of LLMs as assistive tools for SIBT planning under clinician supervision.

items.title: A lightweight deep learning architecture for crack segmentation in structural health monitoring
items.abstract: Automated crack segmentation is a key component of vision-based structural health monitoring for civil infrastructure. However, many deep learning approaches remain computationally demanding for embedded edge devices and exhibit limited generalisation across diverse materials and imaging conditions. This paper presents a lightweight deep learning architecture designed to balance segmentation accuracy, computational efficiency, and cross-domain robustness. The artificial intelligence contribution is an efficient encoder–decoder integrating depthwise separable convolutions, lightweight multi-scale context aggregation, and channel attention. The proposed approach targets crack continuity through a unified design for thin-structure segmentation under strict computational constraints. The engineering contribution is a practical inspection method for structural health monitoring systems with limited memory, latency, and power budgets. Experiments on a joint dataset comprising 30,017 crack images collected from 20 heterogeneous datasets demonstrate competitive performance across diverse conditions. The proposed Lightweight Attention Channel-Enhanced Crack Segmentation (LACE-Crack) architecture achieves a higher harmonic mean of precision and recall (F1 score) (0.569 vs. 0.566), precision (0.751 vs. 0.732), mean intersection over union (0.694 vs. 0.693), optimal image scale (0.489 vs. 0.480), and optimal dataset scale (0.425 vs. 0.411) than the comparison architecture, with comparable recall (0.459 vs. 0.462). It also requires approximately 43% fewer parameters and 64% fewer floating-point operations. These results demonstrate a strong balance between crack segmentation performance and computational efficiency, supporting the practical use of lightweight artificial intelligence for infrastructure inspection under deployment constraints.

items.title: A Literature Review on Artificial Intelligence-Based Speech Intelligibility Assessment in Motor Speech Disorders
items.abstract: This scoping review aimed to examine the methodological characteristics and performance of artificial intelligence (AI)-based speech intelligibility assessment in individuals with acquired motor speech disorders. It also evaluated the clinical applicability of AI-based assessment by reviewing the relationship between AI-based assessments and human perceptual ratings. Four international databases (PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect) and three Korean databases (KISS, DBPIA, and RISS) were searched up to March 2026. Fifteen studies were selected after applying predefined exclusion criteria. The selected studies were classified and synthesized descriptively without risk-of-bias assessment. 1) Reading tasks were the most frequently used speech task across the 15 included studies, regardless of the data collection method. 2) A wide range of automatic speech recognition systems (e.g., Google Cloud ASR API; Google LLC, Mountain View, CA, USA) and machine learning and deep learning models (e.g., bidirectional long-short term memory, convolutional neural networks, support vector machines, and linear regression) were used, with no single approach predominating. 3) Many studies reported strong correlations or high levels of agreement between AI-based assessments and human perceptual ratings, whereas some reported weak correlations or nonlinear relationships. The included studies generally reported positive associations between AI-based and perceptual intelligibility measures, although the performance metrics and models varied considerably across studies. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted with caution in clinical applications.

items.title: A Modern Representation of the Historical Body of Work on Airfoils: NACA Report 824 and Hoerner’s Fluid-Dynamic Lift Revisited with XFOIL, MSES and AVL Through OCR and AI-Agent Automation
items.abstract: Systematic comparisons of the classic airfoil literature with modern codes have been limited less by physics than by the labour of extracting data from scanned charts. This study shows that optical character recognition and an AI agent, working under the author’s direction, can automate this chain: source retrieval, chart calibration, visual data reading, simulation campaigns, quality control and documentation. With this workflow, all 112 section charts of NACA Report 824 and three planform figures of Hoerner’s Fluid-Dynamic Lift were recomputed with XFOIL, MSES and AVL in about 7.5 hours of elapsed time. Lift-curve slopes agree to a median +2.2 % (XFOIL), and the overprediction grows with thickness. Zero-lift angles are too negative in proportion to camber in both codes; transition modelling and tunnel-wall corrections were ruled out as causes. Drag is underpredicted by about 15 % at all Reynolds numbers. The offset vanishes for Ncrit ≈ 5, an effective parameter for surface imperfections or the shared boundary-layer model. Maximum lift is overpredicted, most for thin sections. AVL reproduces Hoerner’s planform data within a few per cent where the flow is attached and the edges are sharp. Automated checks found errors in the source, the codes and the agent’s own work; human verification remains essential.

items.title: A muzzle-based self-enhancing cow recognition method using YOLO and LLM
items.abstract: In the modern era, using the technology of image processing, people are being facilitated in many sectors. Therefore, we have decided to do research on cow recognition using the methods of image processing. Because cows are pretty essential for human beings, and people from the entire world are being facilitated by cows. Because of that reason, many technologies have been invented till now for the cow. Here we have presented an approach to identify the cow. Like the fingerprint of a human, the cow muzzle is also unique. Due to this reason, we can recognize the cow based on the muzzle. To recognize muzzles, we have used Yolo and the Structural Similarity Index (SSI). Image processing is a sector of Artificial Intelligence and data is quite important to train models. Moreover, to train a model for image processing, it is needed to manage a high-configuration computer. But there are many regions in the world where people hardly get such powerful machines. To mitigate this issue, we have introduced a unique method where we do not need a large amount of data for the image processing task. To eliminate the necessity of collecting a huge amount of data, we included a self- enhancing feature, which helps the model to predict accurately and also helps to improve performance by increasing the amount of data. However, without a large amount of data, it will be possible to predict appropriately because of the presence of self-enhancing features. This certain program helps the model to improve its capability for delivering faster responses. LLM is responsible to add the self-enhancing feature. On the other hand, to find out the most suitable Yolo model for our research, we have trained data with three different versions of Yolo: Yolo v7, v8, and v9. We evaluated the performances of these three versions in terms of Precision, Recall, mAP50, and mAP50-95 and found Yolo v9 to be the best among them. It excels with a precision of 0.391, a recall of 0.916, a mAP50 of 0.559, and a mAP50-95 of 0.307.

items.title: A Plug-and-Play Explainable AI Framework in Credit Score Assessment
items.abstract: Credit scoring is fundamental in enabling institutions to distinguish between creditworthy and high-risk borrowers. Thus, robust credit scoring models are essential for effective financial risk management. Artificial intelligence and machine learning have significantly improved the precision of credit decision support systems, however, these models often operate as black boxes, concealing the underlying logic of credit denials or approvals. To address this challenge and meet the demand for financial transparency, explainable AI (XAI) has emerged as a crucial mechanism for generating decisions that are interpretable to both financial institutions and clients. This paper researched contemporary decision support systems (DSS) used in credit risk assessment and proposes a modular, plug-and-play framework with integrated explainability. Six requirements were derived for a robust system design based on a review of existing XAI frameworks. The framework consists of five interconnected components such as data ingestion layer, feature processing module, a supervised predictive model, an explanation layer, and a decision endpoint. Existing studies often focus on individual predictive models or explanation methods, leaving their integration and component interchangeability unspecified. The proposed framework addresses this gap through explicit interfaces that allow predictive models and explanation methods to be replaced independently. The system will operate with both traditional credit data, alternative data, or both. Thus, feature processing is incorporated to distinguish the importance and relevance of the data to credit assessment decisions. Any irrelevant redundant data is not be considered by the model. The contribution of a study is a reusable architectural specification. The proposed XAI framework is designed to serve as a universal template for researchers and financial institutions developing transparent, effective credit scoring systems.

items.title: A prospective randomized study of patient-centered AI for clinical visit preparation
items.abstract: Patients often arrive at brief, time-constrained clinical visits unsure of what to expect or ask, and millions of adults now turn to general-purpose AI chatbots to prepare beforehand. Yet whether conversational AI improves visit readiness remains unclear. We designed a large language model (LLM)-based visit preparation agent to guide patients before an appointment by gathering clinical context, setting visit expectations, providing relevant health information, building a prioritized list of questions for their clinician, and generating a summary. In a prospective consented randomized study in the Google Health app, 802 U.S. adults held 866 health-related conversations with the visit preparation agent (standard or concise variant) or a minimally prompted control chatbot built on the same LLM. The visit preparation agent significantly outperformed the control across blinded clinician evaluations and patient self-reports. In clinician reviews of completed sessions (n = 272), the agent achieved a 16.6% higher rate of comprehensive preparation (67.2% vs. 50.6%; P < 0.05) and an 8.5% higher rate of alignment with patients' health context (98.9% vs. 90.4%; P < 0.01), while maintaining high medical safety and appropriateness across all study arms. Patient post-surveys (n = 460) showed 16.8% higher visit preparedness (73.8% vs. 57.0%; P < 0.01), 14.3% higher confidence in knowing what to ask (81.4% vs. 67.1%; P < 0.01), and 12.0% higher overall satisfaction (74.0% vs. 62.0%; P < 0.05). Clinician and participant metrics were not significantly correlated, indicating that expert review and patient self-assessment capture complementary dimensions of patient-facing AI. These findings suggest that LLM chatbots can safely help patients prepare for clinical visits, with greater benefit when following a structured workflow, and motivate future studies on in-visit communication and clinical outcomes.

items.title: A Review of Changes in Consumer Perceptions of PGC and UGC Visual Marketing for Luxury Brands with AIGC Intervention
items.abstract: The rapid popularization of artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) is reshaping the communication of social visual content for luxury brands. This paper takes professionally generated content (PGC) and user-generated content (UGC) as research objects and explores changes in consumer perceptions of luxury brand visual marketing before and after AIGC intervention. Based on consumer perception theory and luxury marketing theory, the paper defines core concepts such as luxury brand visual marketing, PGC, UGC, AIGC, perceived luxury, perceived craftsmanship, and perceived trust. Taking existing studies on human-produced PGC and human-produced UGC before the popularization of AIGC as a reference, it analyzes the mechanisms and practical limitations of traditional official materials and native user content in three perceptual dimensions, and further discusses the perceptual changes brought by AIGC-assisted brand PGC, AIGC-involved user UGC, and AIGC-led visual marketing materials. The study finds that the influence of AIGC has a dual nature. It improves content production efficiency and visual expressiveness, while also affecting the human craftsmanship narrative and brand authenticity of luxury goods. Its underlying logic follows the mechanism of “production mode-value perception isomorphism” and perceptual spillover: de-humanization on the production side is regarded by consumers as a signal for judging brand value, and this signal spills over from the communication stage to the product level. While empowering communication, it continuously dilutes perceptions of the human craftsmanship value and authenticity of luxury goods. This paper clarifies the logic of perceptual evolution in luxury brand visual marketing under the AIGC environment and provides theoretical reference for brand digital communication practice and subsequent academic research.

items.title: A Review of Fault Diagnosis Technology for Rotating Machinery Based on Deep Generative Models
items.abstract: Fault diagnosis of rotating machinery frequently encounters the compounded challenges of non-stationary operating conditions and small-sample data constraints. Traditional deep learning models often exhibit suboptimal performance when addressing these issues. Deep Generative Models (DGMs) offer innovative solutions by synthesizing high-fidelity data samples, reconstructing latent system states, and modeling complex multimodal data streams. This paper presents a review of rotating machinery fault diagnosis technologies based on DGMs. The state-of-the-art applications of DGMs and their variants, including Deep Autoregressive Models (DARs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Diffusion Models, and Large Language Models (LLMs), are systematically summarized. Specific applications discussed include data generation, domain adaptation and generalization, multimodal data fusion, as well as downstream fault diagnosis and anomaly detection. Furthermore, this review contrasts DGMs with traditional signal processing methods and standard deep learning models. Current limitations are also critically analyzed, focusing on parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategies, interpretability (reliability), and computational efficiency for edge deployment. Finally, future research directions are proposed, emphasizing few-shot or zero-shot learning, robust multimodal data generation, physics-informed hybrid DGM architectures, and the integration of reinforcement learning with DGMs to further enhance diagnostic accuracy in practical scenarios.

items.title: A Review of Implementation Barriers of Design for Safety (DfS) in the Construction Sector
items.abstract: The construction industry continues to record a high rate of occupational accidents despite sustained safety interventions, indicating that conventional reactive approaches are inadequate. A more proactive approach, such as Design for Safety (DfS), is therefore essential. Although Malaysia introduced the OSHCIM 2017 Guidelines and gazetted the Occupational Safety And Health (Construction Work)(Design and Management) Regulations 2024, which elevated DfS to mandatory status, implementation barriers remain insufficiently classified within a coherent theoretical framework. This study addresses this gap through a narrative synthesis that critically classifies and evaluates DfS barriers, reorganised within the Diffusion of Innovation (DOI) theory. An analysis of 66 articles from the Scopus and Web of Science databases identifies five (5) barrier clusters: deficiencies in knowledge, education and competency; legal, policy and liability issues; weaknesses in stakeholder communication and collaboration; organisational culture, cost and contractual constraints; and limitations in tools and technical support, including Building Information Modelling (BIM). The five (5) DOI attributes, namely relative advantage, compatibility, complexity, trialability and observability, are applied to explain why these barriers persist in the post-CDM 2024 Malaysian context. The findings are further cross-validated against the Prevention through Design (PtD) competency framework by Ibrahim et al. (2020), confirming that each barrier cluster corresponds to a core PtD competency element. Overall, this study asserts that DfS success in Malaysia requires a fundamental shift from a culture of minimum compliance to proactive prevention, supported by professional training, mandatory enforcement, and comprehensive digital technology support.

items.title: A Review on AI-Based Process Monitoring and Quality Control for Additive Cladding Technologies in Industrial Component Remanufacturing
items.abstract: With the transition toward global carbon neutrality and a circular economy, remanufacturing technologies for high-value industrial components have gained significant attention. Additive cladding processes such as laser cladding, directed energy deposition (DED), wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM), and plasma transferred arc (PTA) are key solutions for localized structural restoration. However, dynamic melt pool instability and complex thermal histories often induce defects like porosity and microcracks, degrading product reliability. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted multi-sensor monitoring and closed-loop control systems have been introduced to enhance process stability and repeatability. This review comprehensively categorizes additive cladding processes for remanufacturing and explores recent advancements in AI-driven sensing, deep-learning-based defect prediction, adaptive feedback control, and digital twin integration. Finally, critical technical challenges and future perspectives for industrial deployment are discussed.

items.title: A REVIEW ON EMERGING TRENDS AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES IN AQUATIC TOXICOLOGY: FROM CONVENTIONAL ECOTOXICOLOGY TO PREDICTIVE AND INTEGRATED RISK ASSESSMENT
items.abstract: Aquatic toxicology is rapidly evolving from conventional single-contaminant toxicity testing toward an integrated discipline capable of addressing complex chemical mixtures, emerging contaminants, climate-related stressors, and ecosystem-level responses. Aquatic ecosystems are increasingly exposed to pharmaceuticals, pesticides, endocrine-disrupting chemicals, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), microplastics, nanoplastics, nanoparticles, industrial chemicals, antibiotics and transformation products. At the same time, climate change, eutrophication, habitat alteration and changing hydrological conditions can modify contaminant fate, bioavailability and toxicity. Recent advances in high-resolution mass spectrometry, non-target chemical analysis, multi-omics, environmental DNA (eDNA), adverse outcome pathways (AOPs), exposomics, biosensors and artificial intelligence are transforming aquatic toxicology. Emerging research increasingly emphasizes environmentally realistic concentrations, chronic exposure, mixture toxicity, trophic transfer and interactions between chemical and non-chemical stressors. Multi-omics approaches can connect molecular initiating events with physiological and ecological outcomes, while machine learning can assist contaminant identification, toxicity prediction and risk assessment. Micro- and nanoplastics are particularly important because they can act as both toxicants and vectors for other contaminants. Future aquatic toxicology should integrate field observations, laboratory experimentation, computational modelling and real-time environmental monitoring. Standardization, validation, transparency and environmentally relevant experimental designs will be essential for translating technological advances into effective ecological risk assessment and management.

items.title: A Self-Narrative Inquiry into GenAI-Enhanced Chinese Cultural Instruction
items.abstract: Despite the rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in language education, longitudinal practitioner-centred accounts of how teachers' instructional practices and professional competence evolve through sustained GenAI integration in Chinese cultural instruction remain scarce.This self-narrative inquiry examines one pre-service Chinese language teacher's six-month experience of integrating GenAI into adult Chinese cultural instruction at a university.Drawing on 11 reflective journals, pedagogical artefacts, and semi-structured interviews with three peer observer teachers and two professors specialising in Chinese cultural instruction, the study employs Riessman's (2008) thematic narrative analysis within Clandinin and Connelly's (2000) narrative inquiry framework.Findings reveal a developmental trajectory across three qualitatively distinct phases: designing for novelty, designing for function, and designing for integration.Concurrently, the teacher's role evolved from tool user to tool architect, with AI literacy, in-class improvisational responsiveness to technology failure, and the conceptual repositioning of GenAI from pedagogical spectacle to invisible infrastructure developing iteratively through practice.Two design principles were inductively constructed: GenAI task design should target functions irreplaceable by lowerthreshold alternatives, and GenAI-generated content should compensate for the inaccessibility of authentic materials rather than substitute for them.This study contributes a practitioner-centred, longitudinal perspective to the underexplored intersection of GenAI integration and Chinese cultural instruction, and offers empirically grounded design suggestions for instructional practice.

items.title: A study on vocational education students' cognition of human-ai co-creativity: An empirical analysis based on Q methodology
items.abstract: Based on Actor-Network Theory (ANT), this study adopts Q methodology to conduct an empirical exploration of 24 vocational education students, aiming to reveal the internal structure of their cognitive landscape. The experimental results confirm a prominent Middle Collapse phenomenon: the ideal "symmetric co-creative intentionality" is statistically completely absent, and the student group does not form a continuously progressive cognitive spectrum, but presents a drastic structural polarization. The data extract five typical factors, which are clearly divided into two camps: "defensive polarization" (rejecting the status of AI actants to defend subjectivity) and "dependent polarization" (transferring agency to technological black boxes or macro-environments). Topological analysis further shows that there are deep semantic ruptures between different cognitive groups, indicating systemic blockages in the problematization and interessement stages during the "translation" process. The conclusion of this study points out that the current human-AI collaborative cognition of vocational education students does not naturally move toward symbiosis, but is driven by skill-oriented pressure and employment anxiety, falling into an either-or "translation dilemma". This finding reveals the deep cognitive fractures that vocational education faces in cultivating “responsible co-creators” in the intelligent era, and provides key empirical evidence for reconstructing the educational paradigm of human-AI collaboration.

items.title: A Systematic Review of Tools for Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Classification
items.abstract: Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is one of the common mental disorders affecting children and is often diagnosed with an important delay. This neurodevelopmental disorder is usually identified by symptoms such as a deficit in attention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness. There are clinical and data-oriented methods for ADHD diagnosis. Recently, artificial intelligence techniques for ADHD diagnosis have been taken into consideration. In this article, we have reviewed state-of-the-art deep learning and classical machine learning networks using a wide range of neuroimaging, neurosignal and related data, including structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), questionnaires, genome data, mo-tion data, performance tests and game simulation. In addition, we identified common validation methods and analyzed them. As an important aspect for clinicians, the brain regions of ADHD patients identified as discriminative by existing machine learning-based studies are investigated. In the end, we identify exiting research gaps, notably the lack of publicly available large-scale multimodal datasets, non-interpretability and inexplicability of many algorithms and the use of architectures that are unable to efficiently model the spatiotemporal features of the brain. Ultimately, we hope that researchers will implement explainable machine learning-based studies that use several neuroimaging modalities to aid clinicians in supporting their decisions for diagnosis, prognosis and for treatment planning.

items.title: A Teacher Training Model for the Age of AI. Integrating Critical Use and Relational Competences
items.abstract: The spread of artificial intelligence (AI) in educational settings is transforming teaching, learning and the design of school environments (European Commission, 2022; UNESCO, 2023). Alongside the opportunities, questions have emerged regarding the teacher's educational role, which is often overlooked by approaches that focus primarily on AI literacy (Isma'il & Ibrahim, 2025). Against this backdrop, this paper proposes a teacher training model that integrates digital, interpersonal and interpretative competences. The literature highlights how teachers' attitudes towards AI depend not only on their technological skills, but also on the conceptions that shape their professional practice (Cabero-Almenara et al., 2024). Content-transmission approaches tend to be associated with greater resistance to such technologies, whilst perspectives more focused on interpersonal relationships and constructivism interpret them as tools to support learning (Chan & Tsi, 2024). Concerns regarding the spread of AI therefore involve not only technical aspects but also issues of identity linked to the meaning attributed to teaching (Puja et al., 2025). items.title: A Unified XAI-NSAI Analytical Framework for Trustworthy IoT Anomaly Detection
items.abstract: The widespread deployment of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in critical environments makes anomaly detection essential for identifying abnormal behaviors and supporting timely investigation and response. However, accurate detection alone is insufficient. Practical IoT deployments must also provide explanations, incorporate domain knowledge and reasoning, operate under IoT constraints, and support human decision making. Although recently proposed approaches increasingly incorporate Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) or Neuro-Symbolic Artificial Intelligence (NSAI), XAI and NSAI methods are often considered independently. We argue that they should be considered together to better understand their complementary roles in supporting trustworthy IoT anomaly detection. To address this gap, we propose a unified analytical framework organized around five complementary dimensions. The framework provides a structured basis for characterizing existing approaches, identifying capability gaps and design trade-offs, and guiding the design of new anomaly detection systems for different IoT applications. We demonstrate the framework's analytical utility by applying it to three representative studies and illustrate its design utility through its application to a Medical IoT anomaly detection system.

items.title: Accuracy of artificial intelligence versus eyecare practitioners in detecting diabetic retinopathy using retinal fundus images: a systematic literature review
items.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) prevalence rises among low- and middle-income countries where access to appropriate eye care services is lacking. Detecting DR requires retinal fundus imaging, but interpretation conventionally depends on eye-care practitioners, who are affected by shortcomings like inter-observer variability. Artificial Intelligence (AI), a promising technology for automated image examination and interpretation, enables wider, faster screening coverage and consistency. The review compares the diagnostic accuracy of AI and practitioners in detecting DR using retinal images. We conducted a systematic literature review using PRISMA 2020, searching major electronic databases with search terms: diabetic retinopathy, artificial intelligence, eye-care practitioners, and diagnostic accuracy. Eligible studies were published in English, peer-reviewed, and met the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Data extraction, organization, and accuracy were enabled through an Excel data form. The review included 15 of 540 identified studies. AI diagnostic tools like Google’s ARDA show equal or higher accuracy than humans in detecting DR, in some instances, in categorizing images. AI brings hope and assurance in prompt identification, management, and referral. Its performance is limited by the tendency to flag images as false positives; however, this depends on image quality, disease severity, datasets used, and overall grading criteria. Human strength remains in clinical judgement, contextualised interpretation of ungradable or low-quality images, and patient-specific management approach. AI implementation to complement care should be steered by local validation through comparison with eye care givers and approval through standardized protocols, quality control, ethical considerations, and data security.

items.title: Accurate and Auditable ECG Classification via Visibility Graph Neural Networks
items.abstract: Physicians read electrocardiograms (ECGs) from waveform shape and timing, yet accurate deep-learning classifiers rarely show which waveform regions drive their predictions. We introduce LYNX-ECG, a graph neural network that represents each heartbeat as a sparse visibility graph of timestamped turning points. On CODE-Test, LYNX-ECG reaches a macro F1 score of 0.889, outperforming five baselines including the ECGFounder foundation model, while its graphs need about 14% of the storage of graphs built from every sample. Because each node maps to a specific ECG time, we can delete clinically defined waveform regions and alter beat timing to audit predictions. For conduction disorders, the clinically expected region was the strongest evidence in more than 90% of correct predictions. Bradycardia and tachycardia calls follow heart rate with conduction intervals held fixed, and atrial fibrillation calls vanish when beat-to-beat variation is removed. Sparse visibility graphs thus pair accurate ECG classification with clinically grounded, testable explanations.

items.title: Advances in Alzheimer’s disease diagnosis and therapeutic strategies: an integrative review of current evidence.
items.abstract: Alzheimer's disease is the leading cause of dementia worldwide and represents one of the greatest challenges facing contemporary medicine because of its high prevalence, irreversible progression, and profound impact on patients, their families, and healthcare systems. The present study aimed to analyze recent scientific advances in the diagnosis and therapeutic strategies for Alzheimer's disease through an integrative review of specialized literature. To achieve this objective, a qualitative analysis of scientific publications was conducted. The findings reveal a significant transformation in the diagnostic paradigm, shifting from an approach based primarily on clinical assessment to one supported by biological biomarkers, advanced neuroimaging techniques, and precision medicine strategies capable of identifying neuropathological changes during the preclinical stages of the disease. Likewise, the literature demonstrates a substantial shift in treatment approaches, moving from symptomatic management toward interventions designed to modify disease progression. Important advances were also identified in the fields of artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, precision pharmacology, and the development of innovative drug discovery platforms. Although significant challenges remain regarding biological heterogeneity, clinical efficacy, safety, accessibility, and the implementation of these innovations, the available scientific evidence indicates that the future management of Alzheimer's disease will be based on early diagnosis, molecular patient stratification, and the development of personalized therapeutic strategies capable of delaying neurodegeneration and improving clinical outcomes.
